theater: 敘利亞北部地中海沿岸烏加里特

battle.name: 烏加里特的毀滅
battle.theater: 敘利亞北部地中海沿岸烏加里特
battle.brief: 公元前1190年前後，烏加里特在青銅時代末期的崩潰中被毀：王宮區同街區同時焚毀，港口與陸路一併受制，國家行政同文字傳統中斷。攻方身分至今存疑，或與「海上民族」及「圖魯」之地的軍隊有關。埃及的青銅、黃金同象牙支撐著這座城，埃及長矛體系亦隨商隊抵達，毀滅層的埃及器物正是往來的最後痕跡。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 烏加里特王國的毀滅沒有留下任何一份戰役報告，戰場上的兩方只能從考古層位同殘存書信還原。防守的一方是敘利亞海岸的烏加里特王國：全盛期為青銅時代中晚期的黎凡特大城邦，疆域不廣，卻握有地中海東岸最好的深水港之一，壟斷紫檀木、香木、穀物、橄欖油同銅料的轉口生意。軍隊以王宮警衛隊為核心，下轄步兵、弓箭手同雙輪輕戰車隊；王權集中於王宮一處，命令靠書吏傳遞的王室文書下達，沒有像埃及那樣龐大的常備軍同兵役制度。進攻的一方身分未定，學界並列數種說法：其一，認為是「海上民族」的聯盟，即從安納托利亞南部、塞浦路斯、克里特、西利西亞同薩丁尼亞方向來的集團；其二，以烏加里特殘存書信中出現的「圖魯之地國王」為主，指安納托利亞南部的軍隊；其三，認為是本地衰落城邦的殘餘勢力。埃及在這場衝突裡的位置同樣有爭議：拉美西斯三世時代的埃及在敘利亞海岸設有分遣隊同商站，梅迪奈特哈布的浮雕把「海上民族」聯盟畫得清楚，卻沒有提到烏加里特，因此部分學者認為埃及只作壁上觀，另一部分則主張埃及曾組建聯盟出手，烏加里特是其棋子。文書上唯一可以確定的是：攻方來自海上或陸地的西北方，而且不是一次可以輕易重複的劫掠。
countriesEn: The destruction of Ugarit left no battle report of any kind, so the two sides on the field can be reconstructed only from the archaeological strata and the surviving letters. The side that defended was the kingdom of Ugarit, a great Levantine city-state of the middle and late Bronze Age on the Syrian coast. Its territory was not large, but it held one of the best deep-water harbours on the eastern Mediterranean and controlled the transhipment of hagarwood, fragrant woods, grain, olive oil and copper. Its army was built around the palace guard, with foot soldiers, archers and a corps of light two-wheeled chariots; authority was concentrated in the palace, orders travelled on paper in the form of royal documents, and the kingdom had nothing like the mass standing army or the service system of Egypt. The identity of the attackers is not settled, and scholarship lists several possibilities. The first is a coalition of the so-called Sea Peoples, groups arriving from southern Anatolia, Cyprus, Crete, Cilicia and Sardinia. The second takes the king of the land of Turu, named in a surviving Ugaritic letter, to be the leader of an army from southern Anatolia. The third sees the work of the remnants of local, declining city-states. Egypt's position in the conflict is equally disputed. Egypt of the reign of Ramesses III kept detachments and trading stations on the Syrian coast, and the reliefs of Medinet Habu show the coalition of the Sea Peoples in clear detail without ever naming Ugarit, so some scholars hold that Egypt only watched from the wall, while others argue that Egypt organised a coalition of its own and that Ugarit was a piece on that board. What the documents do fix is this much: the attack came from the north-west by sea and by land, and it was not a raid that could easily be repeated.
people: 能點名的只有烏加里特王室。末代君主之一是阿米施塔姆魯二世，他的祖父尼克馬杜二世曾同埃及第十八王朝聯姻，把女兒嫁給圖特摩斯三世，那是烏加里特最盛的年代；王宮檔案裡還出現過阿米施塔姆魯二世之弟阿馬姆魯的名字，以及總督家族潘納穆瓦、亞西布-達努等一連串以「阿穆瓦」結尾的書記同官吏姓名。有一封被稱為「寡婦的信」的書簡最為著名：一位王后指認自己的繼子在前任國王死後圖謀不軌，信中提到「圖魯之地的國王」以及來自北方的戰事，這封信通常被排在王國末年，是把烏加里特末日的處境連到外敵上的關鍵文本。進攻方的指揮者完全無名：沒有王名，沒有銘文，沒有戰報，只在考古層位裡留下痕跡，唯一能確定的是攻勢自西北而來，由海路同陸路同時施壓。埃及方面，同烏加里特有直接往來的是梅尼普塔同拉美西斯三世兩朝：梅尼普塔的碑銘提到沿海地區的「西方人」進入迦南，拉美西斯三世則在底比斯的王陵裡把那些敵人刻成浮雕，連同盟者的名號都留了下來；浮雕的匠人不會寫戰史，卻把隊伍的樣子、盾牌同兵器照實畫了出來，可以同烏加里特出土的實物互證。至於誰在城牆上指揮抵抗，史料一片空白。
peopleEn: Only the royal house of Ugarit can be named. One of the last rulers was Ammistamru II; his grandfather Niqmaddu II had married into the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt by sending his daughter to Thutmose III, and that was the height of Ugaritic power. The palace archives also preserve the name of Ammistamru's brother Yamamrul, and a run of scribal and administrative names from the family of the governor Panamuwa, Yassubu-Danu and others, all ending in the surname -amuwa. The most famous document is the so-called widow's letter: a queen accuses her stepson of plotting against the king after the death of her husband, and the text mentions the king of the land of Turu and warfare coming from the north. It is usually placed in the last years of the kingdom and is the key text that ties the situation of Ugarit at the end to an enemy from outside. Nothing at all names the commanders of the attackers. There is no royal name, no inscription and no despatch, only traces in the archaeological strata, and the only certainties are that the blow came from the north-west and that sea and land were pressed at the same time. On the Egyptian side, the direct contact with Ugarit ran through the reigns of Merneptah and Ramesses III. The stele of Merneptah records the westerners entering Canaan along the coast, and Ramesses III had those enemies carved in relief in his royal tomb at Thebes, down to the names of their allies; the craftsmen who cut the reliefs were no chroniclers, but they recorded the shape of the formations, the shields and the weapons truthfully, and those images can be checked against the objects excavated at Ugarit. As for who commanded the resistance from the walls, the sources are simply blank.
kits: 卡面上這件埃及長矛，是早王朝時期的直刃長矛：銅或青銅矛頭以榫口或縛紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩。公元前二千年末到前一千二百年，這件兵器仍然是埃及步兵最省事的主兵器，傭兵同徵召兵用它列成前排，替後面的弓手擋住飛矢。烏加里特同埃及的往來是雙向的：埃及的青銅、黃金、玻璃同象牙經商船抵達烏加里特，烏加里特的香木、穀物同橄欖油走海路運往埃及，王宮區的埃及式莊園同城內的塞沙特神廟說明埃及人在這座城有常住的社群同軍事存在，埃及的長矛體系正是隨這些人同貨物一起抵達的。烏加里特自己的武備另有面貌：雙輪輕戰車由兩匹馬牽引，車上載一至二人，銅矛、銅斧同短劍是近戰主力；圓形木胎蒙皮盾直徑約八十至九十公分，銅包邊並帶中央銅釘；弓為複合弓，箭鏃用銅、骨或燧石；投石索同石彈亦在配備之列。到了青銅時代末期，敘利亞同安納托利亞已開始少量使用鐵製品，仍屬新法的嘗試。海上的部分同樣關鍵：商船、戰船同護航都靠人力划槳加上帆，港口的繫船石、防波堤同碼頭決定攻方能靠岸多少人；烏加里特從未修築環城的高牆作長期抵抗，其城防核心是王宮區的圍牆、壕溝同北側的斜坡。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a straight-bladed weapon of the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder. Between the end of the second millennium and about 1200 BC the weapon was still the most economical main arm of the Egyptian infantry, with mercenaries and levies drawing it up in the front rank to shelter the archers behind them from stray arrows. The traffic between Ugarit and Egypt ran both ways: Egyptian bronze, gold, glass and ivory reached Ugarit by merchant ship, while the fragrant woods, grain and olive oil of Ugarit went to Egypt by sea, and the Egyptian-style estates in the royal quarter together with the temple of Seshat in the city show that there was an Egyptian community resident there with a military presence, and it was with these people and these goods that the Egyptian spear system arrived. The Ugaritic armament had a different character of its own. The light two-wheeled chariot was drawn by two horses and carried one or two men; bronze spears, bronze axes and short swords were the close-combat core. The round shield had a wooden body covered in hide, about eighty to ninety centimetres across, edged in bronze and fitted with a central bronze boss. The bow was a composite bow with arrowheads of copper, bone or flint, and slings and sling stones also formed part of the equipment. By the end of the Bronze Age, Syria and Anatolia were already using a small quantity of iron, still as an experiment in a new technique. The maritime side mattered just as much: merchants' ships, warships and their escort were moved by oar and sail, and the mooring stones, breakwater and quays of the harbour determined how many of the attackers could make the shore. Ugarit never built a circuit wall for a long stand; the heart of its defence was the enclosure wall, the ditch and the northern glacis of the royal quarter.
tactics: 從發掘層位能還原出的是攻與守的骨架。守方把重點放在王宮區：宮牆、壕溝同通往城門的斜坡構成核心防線，港口則用繫船石同石砌突堤限制敵船直接靠岸；因為烏加里特沒有可以讓全軍退守的環城高牆，必須靠城牆、房屋同街巷逐段爭奪。進攻方很可能採取海陸並行：船隊沿海岸逼近，陸上部隊自西北方向切入，兩面夾擊，截斷城同腹地之間的陸路通道，同時奪取港口作為登陸點。城破之後的痕跡尤其清楚：整座王宮區、沿街的作坊區同西部的街區在同一時段焚毀，火勢不是自然蔓延的樣子，而是人為縱火後任由火燒的結果；王室大批的青銅器、象牙雕件同石雕在火中變形或被熔毀，說明攻方並非只想驅走守軍，而是要毀掉這座城市的生產能力同象徵。守方在圍困階段的處境也很可能惡化：糧食靠內陸運入，一旦西北方向的陸路被切斷，城市很快陷入短缺；城內發現的武器數量同種類，包括銅矛、斧、短劍、箭鏃，顯示守軍曾經逐戶抵抗到最後。最後一步也許是撤退：一艘載滿象牙同玻璃的商船在烏加里特外海沉沒，貨物多半是要轉運走的；若城破之際海上通道已經混亂，逃亡的船隻失事便不難理解。城址此後再未重建。
tacticsEn: What the excavated strata allow is the skeleton of the attack and the defence. The defenders concentrated on the royal quarter: the palace wall, the ditch and the ramp leading to the city gate formed the core of the defence, while the harbour used mooring stones and stone-built projections to keep enemy ships from coming directly alongside, and since Ugarit had no wall enclosing the whole city in which the garrison could withdraw for a long stand, ground had to be fought for by wall, house and street lane. The attackers probably combined sea and land. A squadron worked along the coast while troops on the ground cut in from the north-west, closing the land road between the city and its hinterland while taking the harbour as a landing place. The traces of what followed the breach are especially clear. The entire royal quarter, the workshop quarter along the street and the western quarter all burned in the same phase, and the pattern is not that of fire spreading by itself but of a deliberate conflagration allowed to run; large numbers of bronze vessels, ivory carvings and stone sculpture were deformed in the fire or melted down, which tells us the attackers did not merely want to drive off the garrison but to destroy the productive capacity and the symbols of the city. The defenders' situation in the siege would have worsened: grain came overland from the interior, and once the north-western road was cut the city ran short quickly. The quantity and variety of weapons found inside, bronze spears, axes, short swords and arrowheads, show that the defenders fought street by street to the end. The last step may have been flight. A merchant vessel loaded with ivory and glass sank off Ugarit, and the cargo was plainly intended for transport elsewhere; if maritime traffic was already confused when the city fell, it is easy to understand how an escaping ship came to wreck. The site was never rebuilt afterwards.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：中文的戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前1190年；考古上一般以王宮區的第三次毀滅層為準，年代多落在前1190至前1180年之間，較早的說法曾放到前1210年，較遲的說法則推到前1150年。相關的兩個外部錨點是：拉美西斯三世的王名同其在梅迪奈特哈布的戰役浮雕，一般排在公元前1180年代；至於阿卡德王同「圖魯」交戰的史詩《別西卜之歌》，則常被拿來對照烏加里特在更早時面對的安納托利亞方向。第二類是規模：烏加里特城址的面積約二十五至三十公頃，王宮區本身佔數公頃，考古發掘自1939年起歷經數十年；城內人口一般估在兩萬上下，這是根據城面積、房屋密度同碑刻中的行政數字所做的粗略推算，並無普查可依；梅迪奈特哈布的戰役場景中，埃及同其盟軍的方陣被刻得很大，但那屬於繪畫同象徵，不能當作人數。第三類是文物：從王宮區火燒層中搶救出的書寫材料達數千片泥板同數百件文書，另有上百件青銅器、象牙雕件同各式首飾被逐一記錄在案；城外的沉船出水了大量象牙原料、青銅工具同玻璃錠。雙方出動的兵員人數沒有任何可靠文獻可以核實，烏加里特書信裡出現過要求增派部隊的記載，但那只是若干卒伍級的數目，不等於全軍規模。任何寫下「守軍三千、攻軍五萬」一類數字的說法，都應打折扣看待。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology. The Chinese list of battles ties this event to 1190 BC; archaeologically the reference is the third destruction stratum of the royal quarter, which is usually dated between 1190 and 1180 BC, though an earlier view put it at about 1210 BC and a later one pushed it as far as 1150 BC. Two external anchors are relevant. The royal names of Ramesses III and his campaign reliefs at Medinet Habu are usually placed in the 1180s BC; and the Ugaritic epic of the king of Akkad and his fight with the Turu, the Song of Baal-Zeb, has long been used for comparison with the Anatolian threat Ugarit faced at an earlier date. The second class is scale. The site of Ugarit covered roughly twenty-five to thirty hectares, the royal quarter alone took several hectares, and excavation has run from 1939 over several decades. The population of the city is generally estimated at around twenty thousand, a rough inference from the area of the site, the density of housing and administrative figures on the tablets, with no census behind it. In the battle scenes of Medinet Habu the Egyptian and allied formations are cut very large, but that is painting and symbolism and cannot be used as a headcount. The third class is the objects. Thousands of written tablets and several hundred documents were recovered from the burnt levels of the royal quarter, together with catalogues of hundreds of bronze objects, ivory carvings and ornaments of every kind, and the wreck off Ugarit yielded large quantities of raw ivory, bronze tools and glass ingots. The number of men engaged on either side cannot be verified from any reliable document. Ugaritic letters do record requests for additional troops, but those are numbers of a few companies and not the size of a field army. Any account that sets down three thousand defenders against fifty thousand attackers should be taken with a heavy discount.
cause: 毀滅的原因分遠因同近因。遠因是青銅時代晚期體系的鬆動：赫梯帝國在公元前十三世紀末崩解，塞納河流域出現權力真空；愛琴海在宮廷藝術崩壞同地震之後一蹶不振；沿海的城邦個個縮小，文字傳承、冶金傳統同行政制度都開始斷層。烏加里特是這個體系裡依賴最深、也最富的節點之一：它的商路橫跨安納托利亞、塞浦路斯、黎凡特同埃及，港口的收入支撐著王宮的工匠、學士同宮廷開支，一旦這條線被切斷，王室既無力養兵，也無法維持行政。另一層原因是內部的張力：烏加里特同阿馬爾諸城訂立的條約把王國綁在埃及的體系裡，而埃及在拉美西斯王朝末年已自顧不暇，第二中間期的衰弱使烏加里特失去了靠山。近因則是外敵的推進：殘存書信提到北方同西北方向的戰事，以及「圖魯之地國王」的軍隊逼近，這說明攻擊不是孤立事件，而是一整個崩潰期裡從西邊壓過來的一股洪流。最後還有一個內在因素：烏加里特的城防設計以商利為先，沒有環城高牆，一旦港口同陸路同時受制，守軍可退可守的空間有限。
causeEn: The reasons for the destruction divide into distant and immediate causes. The distant cause is the loosening of the Late Bronze Age system. The Hittite empire fell apart at the end of the thirteenth century BC and a vacuum opened in the upper Euphrates; the Aegean collapsed after the ruin of its court art and after earthquakes; the coastal city-states shrank one by one, and their traditions of writing, metallurgy and administration began to break. Ugarit was among the richest and most deeply embedded nodes of that system. Its trade routes ran across Anatolia, Cyprus, the Levant and Egypt, and the income of the harbour supported the craftsmen, scholars and household of the court; once that line was cut the palace could neither pay for soldiers nor keep an administration going. A second layer of cause lies in internal strain. The treaty that tied Ugarit to the cities of the Amurru bound the kingdom to the Egyptian system, and Egypt was unable to look after itself by the end of the Ramesside dynasty, so Ugarit lost the support it had relied on. The immediate cause is the advance of the enemy. The surviving letters speak of warfare in the north and the north-west and of the army of the king of the land of Turu drawing near, which shows that the attack was not an isolated event but one wave of a flood coming from the west during a period of general collapse. One last factor lies inside Ugarit itself. Its fortifications were designed for commerce before anything else, and with no circuit wall, once the harbour and the land road were both constrained the space in which the garrison could hold out or fall back was small.
impact: 毀滅的直接後果是整個國家的消失：烏加里特沒有被重建，原址在鐵器時代只剩一個小型聚落，王室的行政機構、書吏傳統同烏加里特語的使用一併中斷，此後已知的最後一批烏加里特語文獻就是毀滅前寫成的。這對黎凡特青銅時代的整體結構影響極大：原先橫跨地中海東岸的港口網路斷裂，烏加里特這樣的中介城市消失之後，貿易集中到更南方的腓尼基城邦，於是提爾同西頓在西元前一千年前後進入擴張期，後來還催生了字母書寫；而原本控制這片海岸的埃及影響力則全面退潮，敘利亞在之後數百年落入舊赫梯疆域的混亂之中，由小亞細亞同阿拉伯方向來的移民集團逐步重組族群，鐵器時代的城邦格局由此奠定。學術上的影響更為直接：1939年考古學家夏西爾在王宮區挖出成片的書寫泥板同大量器物，把烏加里特從一個傳說中的名字變成可讀的文本世界；同時他用鳥瞰式的全面發掘法一次看見整座城市，示範了後世考古的操作方式。對「海上民族」這個說法而言，烏加里特的毀滅既是最有力的物證，也是一個提醒：目前沒有任何一份文本能指認攻方是誰，舊說同新說都仍在爭辯之中。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the destruction was the disappearance of the state. Ugarit was never rebuilt, and only a small settlement remained on the site in the Iron Age; the administrative machinery of the court, the scribal tradition and the use of the Ugaritic language were all interrupted, and the last known Ugaritic documents in fact belong to the period just before the destruction. The effect on the whole structure of the Levantine Late Bronze Age was considerable. The port network that had run across the eastern Mediterranean broke apart; once a mediating city such as Ugarit disappeared, trade concentrated in the Phoenician city-states further south, and Tyre and Sidon entered a period of expansion around 1000 BC, out of which the alphabetic writing of the Phoenicians later grew. Egyptian influence over that coast withdrew entirely, and Syria passed through centuries of confusion among the territories of the old Hittite world before being reorganised by migrant groups from Asia Minor and Arabia, fixing the pattern of the Iron Age city-states. The scholarly effect is even more direct. In 1939 the archaeologist Schaeffer excavated a field of written tablets and a mass of objects in the royal quarter, turning Ugarit from a legendary name into a readable textual world, and at the same time he surveyed the whole city at once by his method of open-area excavation, which demonstrated the operation of archaeology ever afterwards. For the argument about the Sea Peoples the destruction of Ugarit is at once the strongest material evidence and a warning: no text identifies the attackers, and both the old explanations and the new ones are still being argued.
result: 結果非常明確，儘管細節無從補全：烏加里特王國在這場戰爭之後從未重建，王宮區的第三代毀滅層把城址的時代畫上句點，城市的功能、港口的角色同王室的制度都在火裡中斷。攻城者的身分至今未定，進攻的規模、路徑同經過也沒有任何一位參與者的記錄留下；可以確定的只有攻勢來自西北方、港口同陸路同時受制、毀滅是全面而縱火的，並且城市的核心資產被刻意破壞而非被帶走。統治階層隨之消失：書吏、祭司、車隊長同王室成員的群體隨城市一起流散，烏加里特語從此沒有新的使用者，一個延續了三千年的城邦文明在幾代人內退場。此後這塊土地只以「Tell Ras Shamra」之名留在地圖上，直到二十世紀初被重新挖出為止。史學家常把這場毀滅放在青銅時代晚期崩潰的因果鏈末端：它既是帝國崩解的產物，也是崩解本身的加速器，當最富的港口城市先一步燒掉，原本還在勉強維持的區域體系便失去了支點。
resultEn: The outcome is very clear even though the details cannot be filled in. After the war that destroyed it, the kingdom of Ugarit was never rebuilt, and the third destruction stratum of the royal quarter put an end to the site, while the function of the city, the role of the harbour and the institutions of the court were all broken in the fire. The identity of the besiegers remains undetermined, and no participant left any record of the scale, the route or the course of the attack. What can be certain is that the blow came from the north-west, that the harbour and the land road were constrained at the same time, that the destruction was comprehensive and deliberate, and that the core assets of the city were wrecked rather than carried off. The ruling class disappeared with it: the body of scribes, priests, chariot officers and members of the house was scattered with the city, the Ugaritic language found no new speakers, and a civic civilisation that had run for three thousand years retired from the stage within a few generations. Thereafter the place survived on maps only under the name of Tell Ras Shamra, until it was dug up again in the early twentieth century. Historians commonly set this destruction at the end of the causal chain of the Late Bronze Age collapse. It was both the product of the breaking of empires and an accelerator of that breaking: when the richest harbour city burned first, the regional system that was still being held together lost its fulcrum.
